The first two terms have a common factor of $4x^{2}$, so this group can be rewritten as $4x^{2}\left(x + 15y\right)$. The last two terms have a common factor of $y^{2}$, so this group can be rewritten as $y^{2}\left(x + 15y\right)$. Therefore, the expression can be rewritten as $4x^{2}\left(x + 15y\right) + y^{2}\left(x + 15y\right)$. Since both terms have a common factor of $\left(x + 15y\right)$, the expression can be factored as $\left(x + 15y\right)\left(4x^{2} + y^{2}\right)$, which is equivalent to $\left(4x^{2} + y^{2}\right)\left(x + 15y\right)$.
